newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries recover in London, bewail data dearth.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries recover in London, bewail data dearth.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries traded in London were mired as a dearth of economic data left investors unsure of their next move, traders said on Wednesday.
Earlier profit taking in Tokyo was reversed, as the underlying tone remains buoyant and European buying emerged. However, further upside appears limited without momentum from data, they added.
"We're seeing a bit of moving from the 30s to the tens and fives," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London. "Beyond that, people are pretty much where they want to be already."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was at 100-17, yielding 6.58 percent compared with 100-14 in Tokyo and 100-18 at the New York close.
September T-bond futures were up 2/32 at 113-22 in automated trade. Traders said the contract was expected to consolidate at the current high levels, after recently shooting up.
September T-bonds have risen from a low of 105-30 in mid April to a high of 113-31 on July 7.
The major focus for the market was the June producer price data scheduled for release on Friday, with only minor data such as May wholesale trade figures, due at 1400 GMT on Wednesday, on the way.
May wholesale figures are forecast to show a rise of 0.2 percent, compared with a fall of 0.7 percent last time.
Andrew Davies, bond analyst at the London Bond Broking Company here said Treasuries' current mood was too buoyant, and there was not much more for them to do.
"But I'd stay exposed to the dollar which wants to go up further," he said. "Within Treasuries, I don't think the 30 year can do much more."
